recent_posts.Post Message: The Sabin Vaccine Institute announced it has completed enrollment in all six Phase 2 clinical trials for its cAd3-Marburg Vaccine and its cAd3-Sudan Ebolavirus Vaccine candidates.  There are no licensed vaccines for protection against disease caused by Marburg virus or the Sudan virus strain of Ebola. Both are highly contagious hemorrhagic fever diseases that can have a high fatality rate of up to 88%.    Phase 2 clinical trials to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of the two monovalent vaccines, both on the cAd3 platform, began in healthy volunteers in Africa in 2023 and in the United States in 2025. The African trials, with sites in Kenya and Uganda, completed participant follow-up last year and reporting activities are progressing. The U.S. trials completed enrollment last month.  In addition, Sabin’s cAd3-Marburg Vaccine has been used in Phase 2 rapid response outbreak clinical trials in Africa — more than 1,700 participants enrolled in 2024 during an outbreak in Rwanda, and more than 500 participants enrolled beginning last December for Ethiopia’s first-ever Marburg outbreak.   Learn more ⤵️ https://ow.ly/VYva50YrNc7

As the presentations and discussions of the 14th International Conference on Typhoid & Other Invasive Salmonelloses enter their final day in Phnom Penh, we thank everyone who engaged in this week's essential conversations on the future of typhoid prevention.   A special thank you to the generous supporters of this event: Gates Foundation, GSK, Coalition against Typhoid, and Bharat Biotech.

For the International Women's Day #IWD2026 theme of Give to Gain, we asked our Global Immunization team who gave so they could gain in their lives.  ✨ Celebrating all the women who give so generously through mentorship, funding, and support to foster growth for women and girls globally.   #Vaccines Work #HPV #ProtectHerFuture #GiveToGain

top_post.post_message: "There's a vaccine that’s proven very effective at prevention. There is also new advice that actually we can vaccinate girls once and that will offer lifelong protection."  On #InternationalHPVAwarenessDay,  the global effort to #PreventHPV is more active than ever.  Hear from global leaders about efforts to protect against HPV and prevent #CervicalCancer in this "Supporting Women, Ending HPV" playlist of Sabin's Getting to Zero interview series.  🎥: https://ow.ly/3jSL50YoKPN

board.public_perception_text: Sabin's social media presence continues to strengthen institutional reputation. Our messaging reaches diverse stakeholder groups with strong engagement metrics. Positive sentiment reflects public confidence in our vaccine research and immunization initiatives.
board.donor_engagement_text: Social channels serve as critical touchpoints for demonstrating research impact and organizational effectiveness. assumptions: Reach and impressions are standardized into one visibility metric per platform, using impressions when available and otherwise reach.
Report-facing summary cards use Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn only so the dashboard and quarterly report share one scope.
Cross-network post engagements continue to come from Hootsuite's Post engagement aggregate, with X removed when legacy X totals are present.
Detailed platform, program, and post layers continue to use standardized post-level exports where available, and link clicks stay separate from engagement totals.
Owly link-click exports are treated as website-resource traffic enrichment for Facebook and LinkedIn posts; X/Twitter Owly tables are optional when present.
YouTube follower counts remain available in raw Hootsuite exports, but report-facing summary cards exclude YouTube until a matching platform detail layer is maintained.
Actual follower pace uses real January 1 follower counts when they can be recovered from January exports or saved January dashboard artifacts.
Target pace remains a separate benchmark derived from the stated year-end target and annual growth rate.
Monthly export completeness is complete only when the cross-platform aggregate export, all full post-performance exports, and the expected Facebook/LinkedIn Owly website-click exports are present.
Email exports are excluded from social platform calculations to avoid mixing unlike metrics.
Follower pace is labeled slightly behind when actual performance is within 5% of the benchmark pace.

The cross-platform aggregate account_metrics export is the all-platform rollup, and supplemental top-post files may still be needed to support post-level context where full post-performance exports are missing.
